text.tspan: The science climbed while the policy went quiet
Mountains entered the climate regime in 1992, vanished from its two operative agreements, and returned three decades later —
on the back of assessments that had meanwhile given them a chapter, then a cross-chapter paper, of their own.
assessments feed the instruments — but for 18 years the instruments carry no mountains at all
THE EVIDENCE BASE · ALL 25 MOUNTAIN-SPECIFIC AGREEMENTS, BY FAMILY
W. Tien Shan · Central Asia · East African Community · Prespa Park
25 of 1,465 multilateral environmental agreements name mountains — 1.7 per cent. Eighteen of the twenty-five come from two mountain ranges.
of the world's mountain area sits in a
country with a regional mountain treaty
26 of 180 mountain countries · 2.41 of 50.29 M km²
nothing for the Andes, Himalaya, Rockies or Ethiopian Highlands

Mountain references counted in the primary texts: UNFCCC 1992; Kyoto Protocol 1997; Paris Agreement FCCC/CP/2015/10/Add.1; COP27 decision FCCC/SBSTA/2022/L.20/Add.1 para 3; first global stocktake decision -/CMA.5 (2023), para 181 mandating an SBSTA expert dialogue on mountains.

Treaty counts and country coverage recomputed from GEO Mountains (2026), Dataset on the spatialisation of MEAs in mountain regions v1.0, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18386085 (IEA Database, Université Laval). Mountain area after Sayre et al. (2018), K1–K3 union.
